metadata.content: Man City charges: Case involving alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules could drag on for years | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City charges: Case involving alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules could drag on for years Sky Sports News understands that the process around Manchester City case is moving to the appeal stage, after reports claimed that most of the charges against the club for breaking Financial Fair Play rules were found to have been proven Kaveh Solhekol Chief Correspondent Monday 28 September 2026 07:32, UK Manchester City have been embroiled in legal disputes with UEFA and the Premier League for 12 years and they are so determined to clear their name, and the 115 charges case is so big, that it could still be years before the saga is concluded. According to reports last week, an independent tribunal has reached decisions in the case and Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage. In 2014 City paid a £49m fine for breaking UEFA's financial fair play rules and in 2020 they were given a two-year European competition ban and fined €30m for breaking the rules again. The ban was overturned at the Court of Arbitration for Sport where City were cleared of disguising owner funding as sponsorship income.
